elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once in any 12-month period.
elements.evidence: Rendered §3.4: "may, no more than once in any twelve (12) month period and upon no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice" — express 12-month frequency cap on the inspection right.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 30 days' written notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: Retained language: "upon no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice to the Company".
Retained language: "during the Company's normal business hours".

elements.element: Audits are conducted by an independent auditor.
elements.evidence: The inspection is performed by "HDI's General Manager", i.e. Vendor personnel, not an independent third-party auditor; no independent-auditor requirement was inserted.

elements.element: The auditor is bound by confidentiality obligations.
elements.evidence: §3.4 as rendered contains no confidentiality undertaking covering the inspecting person; the clause is silent and no such obligation was added.

elements.element: Audits are conducted off-site where possible.
elements.evidence: No off-site preference appears; the clause simply permits inspection of "the records of the Company's General Manager" with no location constraint.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 5 percent.
elements.evidence: "The fees incurred by HDI in connection with the inspection shall be borne by HDI." — unconditional Vendor cost allocation, at least as favourable as the 5% shift condition.

elements.element: Vendor has no direct access to Customer systems for an audit.
elements.evidence: The right is limited to inspecting "records ... reasonably related to the calculation of such payments"; no system, network or remote-access right is granted anywhere in the cited provision, so no system-access language exists to delete.

elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once per year.
elements.evidence: Inserted cap: "no more than once in any twelve (12) month period".

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 15 days' notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: Existing "no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice" exceeds the 15-day floor.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 10 percent.
elements.evidence: "The fees incurred by HDI in connection with the inspection shall be borne by HDI" — Vendor bears cost with no shift-back trigger at all.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete: the single inserted frequency cap supplies the only missing fallback element, and the retained 30-day written notice and unconditional HDI-borne cost language already satisfy the other two on their operative terms.

Preferred level is not reached because three elements remain absent from operative language: (a) the inspector is "HDI's General Manager" rather than an independent auditor; (b) no confidentiality obligation binds the inspector; (c) no "off-site where possible" limitation. To reach preferred the drafter would need to add an independent-auditor requirement, a confidentiality undertaking by that auditor, and an off-site preference.

No-system-access element is treated as met because the right is confined to inspecting payment-calculation records and the clause grants no direct, remote or on-system access; nothing needed deletion.

Minimality holds: the edit is a single inserted phrase plus the comma required for grammar; the favourable notice, business-hours and cost sentences survive verbatim, and no survival tails, procedures, remedies or extra requirements outside the fallback checklist were added.

Intent preserved: the inspection subject matter, the General Manager references, the payment-calculation nexus and the cost allocation are unchanged; no defined term, cross-reference or retained sentence is left dangling or contradicted.
Finding status "deviation" is supportable — before the edit the clause had no frequency limit at all, failing the fallback and approaching the walk-away "unlimited audits" position.
